newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu warns PLO against declaring state.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu warns PLO against declaring state.

text.p: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday that Israel would respond very severely if the PLO declared a Palestinian state in self-ruled areas of the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

Asked how he would react to a unilateral declaration of Palestinian statehood, Netanyahu told Israel Radio: "If there is a one-sided declaration by the Palestinians concerning the final agreement...we will respond very severely.
"This would be a violation of the agreement."

Netanyahu spoke one day after Palestinian President Yasser Arafat was given a hero's welcome in Hebron, which on Friday became the last of seven West Bank towns to be given Palestinian rule under a 1995 interim peace deal.
Israel and the PLO are to determine the final status of the West Bank and Gaza in negotiations ending no later than May 1999. Netanyahu rejects Palestinian aspirations for statehood.
The Israeli leader said he was encouraged by the tone of Arafat's speech to thousands of cheering supporters in Hebron on Sunday when he said peace had been "settled with all Israelis".
"We welcome the more positive tone. This is a better direction," Netanyahu said.

Israel and the PLO signed the Hebron deal last week ending months of protracted negotiations and arm-twisting by the United States. The accord outlines further withdrawals Israeli troops will make from parts of the West Bank beginning on March 7.
Netanyahu told Israel's army radio the deal ensured that Israel alone would determine the scope of subsequent redeployments.

"We will define the areas we need for maintaining our security and this is also agreed upon by the Americans -- that the side which will determine the scope of (future) redeployments is Israel," he said.
